records.source: בֶּן־שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֥ם אִמּ֖וֹ חֶפְצִי־בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: A son of two [and] ten year[s was] Manasseh when he became king, and fifty and five year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Hephzibah.
pieces: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah.

L.1: Manasseh [was] a son of twelve years when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother [was] Hephzibah.

R.1: Manasseh became king at the age of twelve, and he ruled in Jerusalem for fifty-five years. His mother was Hephzibah.

decisions.choice: a son of twelve years: twelve years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years, as in 8:17.

decisions.choice: fifty-five years: the longest reign of any king of Judah or Israel
decisions.reason: Manasseh followed his father Hezekiah (20:21). His reign is the longest in Kings, and the same verse that gives it its length opens the worst account of any king of Judah. The years may include a time when he shared the throne with his father, since Hezekiah was given fifteen more years after his illness (20:6) and Manasseh was only twelve when he became king.

decisions.choice: Hephzibah: the queen mother, whose name means "my delight is in her"
decisions.reason: As for every king of Judah, the formula names the king's mother (8:26). Her name is a sentence, "my delight is in her"; Isaiah 62:4 uses the same words as a new name for Jerusalem. The written text divides the name into two words and the scribes marked it to be read as one; the name is the same.

decisions.choice: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the accession formula throughout Kings (8:17).

records.heading: Manasseh king of Judah

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּתֽוֹעֲבֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, according to [the] abominations of the nations which dispossessed Yahweh from before [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, following the detestable practices of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.2: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to the abominations of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.2: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He copied the disgusting things that the nations had done before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forced them out of the land for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: did what was evil in Yahweh's eyes: the bad verdict
decisions.reason: The verdict of the regnal formula, as at 8:18. Manasseh's father Hezekiah had received the best verdict of all (18:3-5); the son receives the worst.

decisions.choice: abominations: practices Yahweh detests
decisions.reason: The word is used for what is utterly offensive to Yahweh, especially the worship and customs of the Canaanite nations. Deuteronomy 18:9-12 uses it of the very practices listed in verses 3-6.

decisions.choice: the nations Yahweh drove out: Judah takes up the sins for which the land was taken from them
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 14:24, the nations lost the land because of these practices (Leviticus 18:24-28; Deuteronomy 9:4-5). If Judah does the same, it faces the same end, as verses 10-15 announce.

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, worded the same way at each level throughout Kings.

decisions.choice: abominations (Literal); detestable practices (Balanced); disgusting things (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 14:24. Readable says "out of the land" for "from before", as there.

records.source: וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ אֶת־הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִבַּ֖ד חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֑יו וַיָּ֨קֶם מִזְבְּחֹ֜ת לַבַּ֗עַל וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֲשֵׁרָה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה אַחְאָב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֨חוּ֙ לְכָל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ד אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he returned and built the high places which had destroyed Hezekiah his father, and he set up altars for the Baal, and he made [an] Asherah, as had done Ahab king of Israel; and he bowed down to all [the] host of the heavens and served them.
pieces: He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had destroyed. He set up altars for Baal and made an Asherah pole, as Ahab king of Israel had done. He bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.

L.3: And he again built the high places that Hezekiah his father had destroyed, and he set up altars for the Baal and made an Asherah pole, as Ahab king of Israel had done; and he bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.

R.3: He built again the hilltop shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He set up altars to worship Baal, and he made a pole used to worship Asherah, just as Ahab king of Israel had done. He bowed down to the sun, moon and stars and worshiped them.

decisions.choice: he returned and built: he rebuilt
decisions.reason: "Returned and built" is a Hebrew way of saying "built again". Manasseh undid his father's reform, in which Hezekiah had removed the high places (18:4, 22).

decisions.choice: an Asherah pole, as Ahab king of Israel had done
decisions.reason: Ahab had set up Baal's altar and made the Asherah pole in Samaria (1 Kings 16:32-33). Kings has called Ahab the worst of Israel's kings; now Judah's king is set beside him. The comparison prepares for verse 13, where Jerusalem will be judged by "the plumb line of the house of Ahab". Asherah was a Canaanite goddess, and her symbol was a wooden pole or tree set up beside an altar.

decisions.choice: the host of the heavens: the sun, moon and stars worshiped as gods
decisions.reason: The "host" or army of the heavens is the sun, moon and stars (Deuteronomy 4:19). Israel was forbidden to bow down to them (Deuteronomy 17:3). Their worship was widespread in Assyria, whose vassal Judah was in Manasseh's day, and the northern kingdom had fallen partly for it (17:16). Josiah later removes it (23:4-5).

decisions.choice: high places, Asherah pole (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrines, a pole used to worship Asherah (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these words in Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: the sun, moon and stars
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the host of heaven" means (m3), as Deuteronomy 17:3 does.

records.source: וּבָנָ֥ה מִזְבְּחֹ֖ת בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת־שְׁמִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he built altars in [the] house of Yahweh, of which said Yahweh, In Jerusalem I will put my name.
pieces: He built altars in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the house about which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said, "In Jerusalem I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name."

L.4: And he built altars in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, of which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said, "In Jerusalem I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name."

R.4: He even built altars inside the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This was the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken of when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name in Jerusalem."

decisions.choice: In Jerusalem I will put my name: the promise about the temple
decisions.reason: Yahweh had chosen Jerusalem as the place for his name (1 Kings 8:29; 9:3; 11:36; Deuteronomy 12:5, 11). To put his name there is to claim the place as his own and to be present there to hear prayer. Manasseh sets up altars for other gods in the very house that bears Yahweh's name.

decisions.choice: altars: the altars for the host of heaven of verse 5
decisions.reason: Verse 5 says what these altars were for. Verse 4 first names the outrage, that they stood in Yahweh's own house, and verse 5 adds whom they served and where in the temple they stood.

decisions.choice: the house about which (Balanced); This was the place ... spoken of (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats "the house" so that "about which" plainly refers to the temple and not to Yahweh. Readable makes the relative clause a sentence of its own and adds "even" for the shock of the act.

records.source: וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְכָל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בִּשְׁתֵּ֖י חַצְר֥וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he built altars to all [the] host of the heavens in [the] two courts of [the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: He built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courtyards of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.5: And he built altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courts of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.5: In both courtyards of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, he built altars to worship the sun, moon and stars.

decisions.choice: the two courts of the house of Yahweh: the inner and the outer court
decisions.reason: Solomon's temple had an inner court for the priests, where the altar of burnt offering stood, and an outer court (1 Kings 6:36; 7:12). Manasseh filled both with altars to the stars. Josiah later tears them down (23:12).

decisions.choice: the host of the heavens: the sun, moon and stars
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

decisions.choice: the sun, moon and stars
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: וְהֶעֱבִ֤יר אֶת־בְּנוֹ֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְעוֹנֵ֣ן וְנִחֵ֔שׁ וְעָ֥שָׂה א֖וֹב וְיִדְּעֹנִ֑ים הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִֽיס׃
records.gloss: And he made pass his son through the fire, and he practiced soothsaying and interpreted omens, and he dealt with [a] medium and spiritists; he increased to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, to provoke [him].
pieces: He made his son pass through the fire, practiced fortune-telling and read omens, and consulted a medium and spiritists. He did much evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, provoking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger.

L.6: And he made his son pass through the fire, and he practiced soothsaying and interpreted omens, and he dealt with a medium and spiritists. He did much evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, provoking [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] to anger.

R.6: He burned his own son in the fire as a sacrifice. He told fortunes and read signs to know the future, and he asked mediums and spiritists to get messages from spirits. He did many things that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said were evil, and this made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry.

decisions.choice: made his son pass through the fire: offered his son as a burnt sacrifice
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 18:10 forbids this rite first in its list, and 12:31 shows that it meant burning children to a god. Ahaz had done it before (16:3), and Kings counts it among the sins for which the north fell (17:17). 2 Chronicles 33:6 says Manasseh did it in the Valley of Ben-hinnom. Josiah later defiles the place where it was done (23:10).

decisions.choice: soothsaying, omens, mediums and spiritists: the practices Deuteronomy 18:10-11 forbids
decisions.reason: The words are those of Deuteronomy 18:10-11. The first may be telling fortunes by reading the clouds; the second is reading omens (Genesis 44:5). The medium and the spiritist are people who claimed to call up the spirits of the dead or to gain hidden knowledge from them (Leviticus 19:31; 1 Samuel 28:7). "Dealt with" may mean that he appointed such people at his court; Josiah later removes them (23:24).

decisions.choice: he did much evil, to provoke: the language of Deuteronomy's warnings
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 4:25 and 31:29 warn that Israel would do evil in Yahweh's eyes and provoke him to anger, and that exile would follow. Kings uses the same words of Manasseh, and the sentence of exile comes in verses 10-15.

decisions.choice: soothsaying, interpreted omens, medium, spiritists (Literal); fortune-telling, read omens (Balanced); told fortunes, read signs to know the future (Readable)
decisions.reason: The words used for these practices in Deuteronomy 18:10-11 at each level, with "soothsaying" kept at Literal for the first. Readable explains each practice as it does there.

decisions.choice: him
decisions.reason: The verb "provoke to anger" has no object in Hebrew; the object is Yahweh. Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: burned ... in the fire as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Readable says what "pass through the fire" meant, as at Deuteronomy 18:10.

records.source: וַיָּ֕שֶׂם אֶת־פֶּ֥סֶל הָאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה בַּבַּ֗יִת אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־דָּוִד֙ וְאֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֔וֹ בַּבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֜ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֨רְתִּי֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת־שְׁמִ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he set [the] image of the Asherah that he had made in the house of which said Yahweh to David and to Solomon his son, In the house the this and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all [the] tribes of Israel, I will put my name for ever;
pieces: He placed the carved Asherah image he had made in the house about which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to David and to his son Solomon, "In this house, and in Jerusalem, the city I chose from among all the tribes of Israel, I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name forever.

L.7: And he set the carved image of the Asherah that he had made in the house of which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name forever.

R.7: He made a carved statue of the goddess Asherah and set it up in the temple. This was the temple {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken about to David and his son Solomon. He had said, "I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name in this temple and in Jerusalem forever. I chose Jerusalem out of all the tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: the carved image of the Asherah: an idol of the goddess herself
decisions.reason: In verse 3 Manasseh made an Asherah pole; here it is a carved image of Asherah, perhaps the same object or a statue of the goddess. He set it inside the temple, where the ark had stood for Yahweh's presence. 23:6 tells how Josiah brought it out and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

decisions.choice: in this house and in Jerusalem ... I will put my name forever: Yahweh's promise to David and Solomon
decisions.reason: The words recall what Yahweh said of the temple when Solomon dedicated it (1 Kings 8:16, 29; 9:3) and of Jerusalem as the city he chose (1 Kings 11:13, 32, 36). The promise was given with a condition (1 Kings 9:4-9), and verse 8 recalls it. The image stands where Yahweh's name was to stand forever.

decisions.choice: forever: the quotation runs on into verse 8
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into verse 8, which adds the second half of Yahweh's word: the promise that Israel would stay in the land, and its condition.

decisions.choice: a carved statue of the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: Readable says that Asherah was a goddess and splits Yahweh's words into two sentences.

decisions.choice: house (Literal, Balanced); temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Kings, Readable says "temple" for Yahweh's "house".

records.source: וְלֹ֣א אֹסִ֗יף לְהָנִיד֙ רֶ֣גֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לַֽאֲבוֹתָ֑ם רַ֣ק׀אִם־יִשְׁמְר֣וּ לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת כְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ים וּלְכָל־הַ֨תּוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם עַבְדִּ֥י מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: and not I will add to make wander [the] foot of Israel from the ground which I gave to their fathers, only if they will keep to do according to all that I commanded them and according to all the law which commanded them my servant Moses.
pieces: And I will not again make the feet of Israel wander from the land I gave to their ancestors, if only they will be careful to do all that I have commanded them, all the law that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Moses commanded them."

L.8: And I will not again make the foot of Israel wander from the land that I gave to their fathers, if only they are careful to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the law that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Moses commanded them."

R.8: I will not make the people of Israel wander away from the land I gave their ancestors again. But they must be careful to obey everything I have commanded them. They must obey all the laws that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Moses gave them."

decisions.choice: make the foot of Israel wander: drive Israel from its land
decisions.reason: To make someone's foot wander is to make them homeless, driven from place to place. The promise was that Israel would be settled for good (2 Samuel 7:10). By Manasseh's day the northern tribes had already been carried off (17:6, 23).

decisions.choice: only if they are careful to do: the condition of the promise
decisions.reason: The promise of the land was never without condition (1 Kings 9:4-7; Deuteronomy 28:63-64). The words prepare for verse 9: they did not listen.

decisions.choice: the law that my servant Moses commanded: the law of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: "Law" (torah) means the whole of Yahweh's instruction given through Moses, as in Deuteronomy 1:5 and 1 Kings 2:3. Moses is called Yahweh's servant as at Joshua 1:2 and 1 Kings 8:53.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As set for "Moses the servant of the LORD": Literal says "slave", Balanced and Readable "servant".

decisions.choice: feet; ancestors; the people of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "feet", since English uses the plural for a people's movements, and "ancestors" for "fathers". Readable says "the people of Israel" and splits the condition into separate sentences.

records.source: וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ וַיַּתְעֵ֤ם מְנַשֶּׁה֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אֶת־הָרָ֔ע מִן־הַ֨גּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הִשְׁמִ֣יד יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And not they listened, and led them astray Manasseh to do the evil more than the nations which destroyed Yahweh from before [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: But they did not listen. Manasseh led them astray, so that they did more evil than the nations {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had destroyed ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.9: But they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray to do evil more than the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had destroyed before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.9: But the people did not listen. Manasseh led them to do wrong. They did even more evil things than the nations {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had wiped out to make room for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: they did not listen: the people share the guilt
decisions.reason: The subject turns from Manasseh to the people. They did not keep the condition of verse 8, so the promise of staying in the land no longer protects them. Yet the king who led them is named as the cause.

decisions.choice: led them astray: made them wander from the right way
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause someone to go astray, like a lost animal. It is the opposite of keeping to the way Yahweh commanded.

decisions.choice: more evil than the nations Yahweh destroyed
decisions.reason: The nations of Canaan were destroyed for their practices (verse 2). Judah now goes beyond them, so it has even less claim to the land than they had.

decisions.choice: to make room for
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "destroyed before" Israel meant, as at 1 Kings 21:26.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh by [the] hand of his servants the prophets, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets, saying,

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves the prophets, saying,

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets. He said,

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" someone means through that person as a go-between, as in 1 Kings 14:18.

decisions.choice: his servants the prophets: the prophets of Manasseh's day, not named
decisions.reason: Kings does not name them. 2 Chronicles 33:10, 18 speaks of the seers who spoke to Manasseh in Yahweh's name. The title "his servants the prophets" recurs in Kings at the fall of each kingdom (17:13, 23; 24:2).

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The servant rule of these books: Literal says "slaves", Balanced and Readable "servants". Balanced and Readable say "through" for "by the hand of" (m1).

records.source: יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ הַתֹּעֵב֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה הֵרַ֕ע מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֥וּ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְפָנָ֑יו וַיַּחֲטִ֥א גַֽם־אֶת־יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּגִלּוּלָֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: Because that has done Manasseh king of Judah the abominations the these, he has done evil more than all that did the Amorite[s] who [were] before him, and he has made sin also Judah with his idols,
pieces: "Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these detestable things, doing more evil than all that the Amorites did before him, and has also made Judah sin with his idols,

L.11: "Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these abominations, has done evil more than all that the Amorites did who [were] before him, and has made Judah also sin with his idols,

R.11: "Manasseh king of Judah has done these disgusting things. He has done more evil than the Amorites who lived in the land before him. He has also led the people of Judah to sin by worshiping his idols.

decisions.choice: the Amorites: the peoples of Canaan before Israel
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 21:26, "Amorites" stands for all the nations who lived in the land before Israel (Genesis 15:16). Genesis 15:16 speaks of the Amorites' wrongdoing coming to its full measure before they lost the land; now Judah's king outdoes them.

decisions.choice: idols: a scornful word for false gods
decisions.reason: The word is used in contempt, as at 1 Kings 15:12 and 21:26. It may be related to a word for dung, though its origin is not certain.

decisions.choice: because ... therefore: the charge in verse 11, the sentence in verses 12-15
decisions.reason: The prophets' word has the shape of a judgment speech: first the charge ("because ..."), then the sentence ("therefore ...", verse 12). The sentence runs on into verse 12.

decisions.choice: made Judah also sin: as Jeroboam made Israel sin
decisions.reason: Kings says over and over that Jeroboam "made Israel sin" (1 Kings 14:16; 2 Kings 17:21-22), and the north fell for it. "Also" sets Judah beside Israel: Manasseh has done to Judah what Jeroboam did to Israel.

decisions.choice: detestable things (Balanced); disgusting things (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: separate sentences without "because" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable states the charges as sentences of their own and joins them to the sentence in verse 12 with "So". Readable adds "lived in the land" to say who the Amorites were (m1), and "by worshiping" to say how the idols led Judah to sin.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וִֽיהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ כָּל־שֹׁ֣מְעָ֔הּ תִּצַּ֖לְנָה שְׁתֵּ֥י אָזְנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: therefore thus says Yahweh God of Israel, Behold I [am] bringing disaster on Jerusalem and Judah, which every [one] hearing it, will tingle both his ears.
pieces: therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Look, I am about to bring such disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that it will make both ears of all who hear of it tingle.

L.12: therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing disaster on Jerusalem and Judah, at which both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.

R.12: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: Listen! I am about to bring a disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that is so shocking that it will make the ears of everyone who hears about it ring.

decisions.choice: both ears will tingle: news so dreadful that it stuns the hearer
decisions.reason: The same words were spoken to Samuel about the fall of Eli's house and the loss of the ark (1 Samuel 3:11); Jeremiah 19:3 uses them of Jerusalem again. What once fell on Shiloh and the priests will now fall on Jerusalem itself.

decisions.choice: I am bringing: an action about to happen
decisions.reason: The participle after "look" describes something already set in motion, as in 1 Samuel 3:11.

decisions.choice: everyone who hears of it: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have a slightly different form of the word "hearing", and the scribes marked another to be read aloud (qere). Both mean everyone who hears of the disaster.

decisions.choice: disaster: harm, calamity
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "evil" in verses 2, 6, 9 and 15. Judah's evil brings evil on it in return: disaster as the fruit of wrong.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD / the LORD says this / This is what the LORD says
decisions.reason: The messenger formula as worded at each level in these books. The tingling ears are worded as in 1 Samuel 3:11 at each level.

records.source: וְנָטִ֣יתִי עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֵ֚ת קָ֣ו שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וְאֶת־מִשְׁקֹ֖לֶת בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב וּמָחִ֨יתִי אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־יִמְחֶ֤ה אֶת־הַצַּלַּ֨חַת֙ מָחָ֔ה וְהָפַ֖ךְ עַל־פָּנֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And I will stretch over Jerusalem [the] line of Samaria and [the] plummet of [the] house of Ahab; and I will wipe Jerusalem as wipes [one] the dish, he wipes and turns [it] on its face.
pieces: I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line used on Samaria and the plumb line used on the house of Ahab. I will wipe Jerusalem clean as someone wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down.

L.13: And I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plumb line of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes the dish: he wipes [it] and turns [it] over on its face.

R.13: I will measure Jerusalem with the same line I used for Samaria and the same plumb line I used for Ahab's family. Jerusalem will meet the same end they did. I will wipe Jerusalem clean, the way someone wipes out a dish and turns it upside down.

decisions.choice: the measuring line of Samaria and the plumb line of the house of Ahab: Jerusalem judged by the standard that brought Samaria and Ahab's house down
decisions.reason: A builder's measuring line and plumb line test whether a wall is straight. Stretched over a city by Yahweh they mean judgment and ruin (Isaiah 34:11; Lamentations 2:8; Amos 7:7-9). Samaria fell to Assyria (17:6) and Ahab's whole house was wiped out (10:10-11); Jerusalem will be measured by the same standard and meet the same end.

decisions.choice: wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a dish, turning it upside down: clear it out completely
decisions.reason: A dish is wiped clean of every scrap and turned over to dry, so that nothing is left in it. Jerusalem will be emptied of its people (verse 14).

decisions.choice: he wipes and turns: the picture of the one who wipes the dish
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe the one wiping the dish, not a second act of Yahweh's, though the picture applies to what Yahweh will do to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: used on
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "used on" to show that Samaria and Ahab's house were measured with these tools, not that the tools belong to them.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem will meet the same end they did
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of the line and the plumb line and adds a sentence saying what it means (m1).

records.source: וְנָטַשְׁתִּ֗י אֵ֚ת שְׁאֵרִ֣ית נַחֲלָתִ֔י וּנְתַתִּ֖ים בְּיַ֣ד אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָי֥וּ לְבַ֛ז וְלִמְשִׁסָּ֖ה לְכָל־אֹיְבֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will forsake [the] remnant of my inheritance and give them into [the] hand of their enemies, and they will become plunder and spoil to all their enemies,
pieces: I will abandon what is left of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own people and hand them over to their enemies, and they will become plunder and spoil for all their enemies,

L.14: And I will forsake the remnant of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance and give them into the hand of their enemies, and they will become plunder and spoil to all their enemies,

R.14: I will abandon those who are left of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own people and hand them over to their enemies. All their enemies will rob them and carry off what they own.

decisions.choice: the remnant of my inheritance: Judah, all that is left of Yahweh's own people
decisions.reason: Israel is Yahweh's inheritance, the people he took as his own possession (Deuteronomy 9:29; 32:9; 1 Kings 8:51). After the northern tribes were carried off, Judah was the remnant left (17:18).

decisions.choice: I will forsake: the reverse of an old promise
decisions.reason: Samuel had said that Yahweh would not forsake his people for his great name's sake (1 Samuel 12:22), and Solomon prayed that he would not forsake them (1 Kings 8:57). The same verb now announces that he will leave them to their enemies.

decisions.choice: give them into the hand of their enemies: hand them over to their power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power, as at 8:20.

decisions.choice: all their enemies: the sentence runs on into verse 15
decisions.reason: Verse 15 gives the reason for the sentence, so the sentence continues there.

decisions.choice: what is left of my own people (Balanced); those who are left of my own people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "remnant of my inheritance" is (m1).

decisions.choice: will rob them and carry off what they own
decisions.reason: Readable puts "plunder and spoil" as plain verbs.

records.source: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶת־הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וַיִּהְי֥וּ מַכְעִסִ֖ים אֹתִ֑י מִן־הַיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצְא֤וּ אֲבוֹתָם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וְעַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: because that they have done the evil in my eyes, and they have been provoking me from the day which came out their fathers from Egypt and until the day the this.
pieces: because they have done what is evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight and have kept on provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger from the day their ancestors came out of Egypt until this day."

L.15: because they have done the evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes and have been provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger from the day that their fathers came out of Egypt even to this day."

R.15: This will happen because they have done what I say is evil. They have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry from the day their ancestors left Egypt until today."

decisions.choice: from the day their fathers came out of Egypt until this day: the whole history of the people
decisions.reason: The charge reaches past Manasseh to the people's whole history since the exodus (17:7). Manasseh's sin fills up a long record of wrong; it does not stand alone.

decisions.choice: have been provoking: a lasting pattern
decisions.reason: The verb "to be" with the participle describes something that has gone on over time, not one act.

decisions.choice: did the evil in my eyes / what is evil in my sight / what I say is evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula of verse 2, here in Yahweh's own mouth. Readable adds "This will happen" to tie the reason to the sentence of verses 12-14, since Readable ended verse 14 with a full stop.

records.source: וְגַם֩ דָּ֨ם נָקִ֜י שָׁפַ֤ךְ מְנַשֶּׁה֙ הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־מִלֵּ֥א אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם פֶּ֣ה לָפֶ֑ה לְבַ֤ד מֵֽחַטָּאתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱטִ֣יא אֶת־יְהוּדָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And also blood innocent shed Manasseh very much, until that he had filled Jerusalem mouth to mouth, apart from his sin which he made sin Judah, to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh.
pieces: Manasseh also shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem with it from one end to the other. This was besides the sin he led Judah into, so that they did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.16: And Manasseh also shed very much innocent blood, until he had filled Jerusalem from mouth to mouth, besides his sin that he made Judah sin, to do the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: Manasseh also killed so many innocent people that their blood filled Jerusalem from one end to the other. And besides that, he led the people of Judah to sin, so that they did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil.

decisions.choice: shed innocent blood: put innocent people to death
decisions.reason: To shed innocent blood is to kill people who have done nothing to deserve it (Deuteronomy 19:10; Jeremiah 22:17). Kings does not say who they were. They may have included those who stayed loyal to Yahweh and the prophets who spoke against the king (verse 10; Jeremiah 2:30). 24:4 says that Yahweh would not pardon this blood.

decisions.choice: from mouth to mouth: from one end to the other
decisions.reason: As at 10:21, "mouth to mouth" means from one opening to the other, completely full.

decisions.choice: besides his sin that he made Judah sin: the bloodshed is a second charge
decisions.reason: The killing is added to the false worship of verses 3-9; both together are given as the reasons for the fall of Judah (23:26; 24:3-4).

decisions.choice: with it (Balanced); their blood (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what filled the city, the blood named at the start of the verse. Readable says "killed ... innocent people" for "shed innocent blood" (m1).

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, as in verse 2.

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י מְנַשֶּׁה֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְחַטָּאת֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֑א הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Manasseh and all that he did, and his sin that he sinned, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Manasseh, all that he did and the sin he committed, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.

L.17: And the rest of the matters of Manasseh, and all that he did, and his sin that he sinned, [are] they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?

R.17: Everything else that Manasseh did, including the sin he committed, is written in the history of the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah: the royal record of Judah
decisions.reason: As at 8:23, the writer points the reader to the court chronicle of Judah, which has not survived. 2 Chronicles 33:11-19 tells more of Manasseh's reign: he was taken to Babylon in chains by the Assyrians, humbled himself before Yahweh, and was brought back to Jerusalem. Kings says nothing of this and keeps to his sin.

decisions.choice: are they not written ...?: a question expecting "yes"
decisions.reason: The question means "they are written there".

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As for every use of this formula in Kings.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר בְּגַן־בֵּית֖וֹ בְּגַן־עֻזָּ֑א וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Manasseh with his fathers, and he was buried in [the] garden of his house, in [the] garden of Uzza; and reigned Amon his son in his place.
pieces: Then Manasseh rested with his ancestors and was buried in the garden of his palace, the garden of Uzza. His son Amon became king in his place.

L.18: And Manasseh lay down with his fathers, and he was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza, and Amon his son reigned in his place.

R.18: Then Manasseh died and was buried in the garden of his palace, the garden of Uzza. His son Amon became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula of Kings, as at 8:24.

decisions.choice: the garden of Uzza: a burial place outside the royal tombs
decisions.reason: Earlier kings of Judah were buried "with their fathers in the City of David" (8:24; 16:20). Manasseh and his son Amon (verse 26) were buried in a palace garden instead. Who Uzza was is not known; the name may recall Uzziah (also called Azariah, 15:1-7), or some other owner of the garden. Kings does not say why the burial place changed.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula as worded at each level throughout Kings. Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the king's "house".

records.source: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אָמ֣וֹן בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁתַּ֣יִם שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ מְשֻׁלֶּ֥מֶת בַּת־חָר֖וּץ מִן־יָטְבָֽה׃
records.gloss: A son of twenty and two year[s was] Amon when he became king, and two years he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.
pieces: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz, from Jotbah.

L.19: Amon [was] a son of twenty-two years when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother [was] Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.

R.19: Amon became king at the age of twenty-two, and he ruled in Jerusalem for two years. His mother was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz, from the town of Jotbah.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty-two years: twenty-two years old
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

decisions.choice: Meshullemeth from Jotbah: the queen mother and her home town
decisions.reason: As for every king of Judah, the formula names the king's mother (verse 1). Jotbah is named only here. It may be a town in Galilee, or Jotbathah, a stopping place in the wilderness south of Judah (Numbers 33:33); the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the accession formula throughout Kings (verse 1).

records.heading: Amon king of Judah

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, as had done Manasseh his father.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as his father Manasseh had done.

L.20: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as Manasseh his father had done.

R.20: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, just as his father Manasseh had done.

decisions.choice: did what was evil in Yahweh's eyes, as Manasseh his father had done
decisions.reason: The bad verdict, as in verse 2. Amon is measured against his father, as later kings are measured against David or Jeroboam.

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, as in verse 2.

records.source: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּכָל־הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־הָלַ֣ךְ אָבִ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֗ד אֶת־הַגִּלֻּלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָבַ֣ד אָבִ֔יו וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And he walked in all the way which had walked his father, and he served the idols which had served his father, and he bowed down to them.
pieces: He followed every path his father had followed. He served the idols his father had served and bowed down to them.

L.21: And he walked in all the way in which his father had walked, and he served the idols that his father had served, and he bowed down to them.

R.21: He lived the same way his father had lived. He worshiped the idols his father had worshiped and bowed down to them.

decisions.choice: walked in all the way: lived as his father lived
decisions.reason: To walk in a way is to live by it, as at 8:18. Amon took up the whole of his father's practice.

decisions.choice: idols: a scornful word for false gods
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

decisions.choice: followed every path (Balanced); lived the same way (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the road; Readable gives its meaning (m1). Readable says "worshiped" for "served", since the service was worship.

records.source: וַיַּעֲזֹ֕ב אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א הָלַ֖ךְ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he forsook Yahweh God of his fathers, and not he walked in [the] way of Yahweh.
pieces: He abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of his ancestors, and did not walk in the way of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.22: And he forsook {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of his fathers, and he did not walk in the way of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.22: He turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of his ancestors, and did not live the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} wanted.

decisions.choice: forsook Yahweh, the God of his fathers
decisions.reason: To forsake Yahweh is to break the covenant by turning to other gods (Deuteronomy 29:24-25; 1 Kings 9:9). "The God of his fathers" sets Amon against the faith of David and Hezekiah before him.

decisions.choice: the way of Yahweh: the life Yahweh commands
decisions.reason: The way of Yahweh is the path of life he has laid down in his commands (Deuteronomy 8:6; Judges 2:22).

decisions.choice: did not live the way the LORD wanted
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the picture (m2).

records.source: וַיִּקְשְׁר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי־אָמ֖וֹן עָלָ֑יו וַיָּמִ֥יתוּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And conspired [the] servants of Amon against him, and they killed the king in his house.
pieces: Amon's officials plotted against him and killed the king in his palace.

L.23: And the servants of Amon conspired against him, and they killed the king in his house.

R.23: Some of Amon's officials made a plot against him, and they killed the king in his palace.

decisions.choice: the servants of Amon: his court officials
decisions.reason: "Servants" of a king are the officials of his court, as at 12:21, where Joash too was killed by his own officials. Kings does not say why they acted.

decisions.choice: conspired: formed a plot
decisions.reason: The verb means to bind together in a plot, the word used of the plots against Joash (12:21) and against Joram (9:14).

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As set for "the king's servants" in these books. Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the king's "house".

records.source: וַיַּךְ֙ עַם־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַקֹּשְׁרִ֖ים עַל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָמ֑וֹן וַיַּמְלִ֧יכוּ עַם־הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת־יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And struck [the] people of the land all the [ones] conspiring against the king Amon, and made king [the] people of the land Josiah his son in his place.
pieces: Then the people of the land killed all who had plotted against King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.

L.24: And the people of the land struck down all those who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.

R.24: Then the people of the land killed everyone who had plotted against King Amon. They made Amon's son Josiah king in his place.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the citizens of Judah as a body
decisions.reason: As at 11:14-20, the phrase means the free people of Judah, the landholders of the country, as distinct from the court in the palace. They act to keep David's line on the throne, as they did for Joash, and they will do so again for Jehoahaz (23:30).

decisions.choice: Josiah his son: the king foretold in 1 Kings 13:2
decisions.reason: A man of God had named Josiah long before as the king from David's house who would tear down the altar at Bethel (1 Kings 13:2; 2 Kings 23:15-16). The worst reign is followed by the coming of the best king (23:25).

decisions.choice: the people of the land (every level)
decisions.reason: As at 11:14, the phrase is kept at every level, since it names a group with a role of its own in Judah (m1). Readable says "They" the second time.

records.source: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָמ֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Amon which he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Amon, what he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.

L.25: And the rest of the matters of Amon that he did, [are] they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?

R.25: Everything else that Amon did is written in the history of the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

records.source: וַיִּקְבְֹּ֥ראֹת֛וֹ בִּקְבֻרָת֖וֹ בְּגַן־עֻזָּ֑א וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And [one] buried him in his grave in [the] garden of Uzza; and reigned Josiah his son in his place.
pieces: Amon was laid in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah became king in his place.

L.26: And [someone] buried him in his grave in the garden of Uzza, and Josiah his son reigned in his place.

R.26: Amon was buried in his own tomb in Uzza's garden, and his son Josiah became king after him.

decisions.choice: one buried him: he was buried
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it means simply that he was buried. The usual death formula ("lay down with his fathers") is missing, perhaps because Amon died by violence.

decisions.choice: the garden of Uzza
decisions.reason: Where his father Manasseh was buried (verse 18).

decisions.choice: [someone] buried him (Literal); was laid (Balanced); was buried (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the unnamed subject; Balanced and Readable use the passive and name Amon.
